label: Face
description: One visible feature of a person's face: its shape, eyes, brows, nose, mouth, jaw, cheeks, forehead, ears or the marks and texture of the skin. Fits the person's drawn age.
notes: Every value of the person.feature lists but their plain ones, one piece at a time. A slot bound to this list ("a boy with <face>") is one whole face: each variant gets pieces of three or four different parts (writer.pieces: its core and the rest as ideas) and the writer's note tells it to describe them as one plausible face in plain words. Named features stacked as a list caricature on some image models, so the pieces stay subtle and the writer says them the way a person describes someone, never as anatomy. Pieces rated strength 2 (marked), and pieces of the aspects compose.asked_only names (what no one notices of a face they saw: nostrils, the groove above the lip, pores and blemishes, earlobes, lashes, the face's proportions), are drawn only when the user picks them. Never praise ('pretty', 'striking'): every piece says what is visible. A piece only one sex has is drawn only when the person's presentation says which (where={"presentation": ...}). The chooser shows the face as its parts, each part its own list (piece), in this list's order of parts.

writer.note: This part is the whole face of someone in the prompt: each variant is one plausible face in three or four features, said the way someone would describe a person they saw: "freckled cheeks, a gap in his front teeth and thick dark brows", "deep-set gray eyes, a long, crooked nose and a weathered, lined face". Its core and ideas are hints in clinical words: never copy them; keep what someone would notice and say it in plain everyday words ("slightly close-set eyes" -> "close-set eyes"), leave out what no one says of a face they saw, and use "slightly" or "gently" at most once. Every feature fits that person as the prompt has them: their age, sex and heritage. An older person's face shows their age in at least one feature ("a weathered, deeply lined face"). No anatomical terms, no praise; no expression, hair, makeup or anything they wear. Start with a feature that needs no "a" or "the" ("freckled cheeks", "deep-set eyes", "weathered skin"). 8 to 16 words.
